title: Refusing Europe unless paid $1,500 a week
summary: After a dangerous smoky cave, Sam says he will not go back to Europe except for $1,500 plus hotel.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That's why they've got you playing in those dumps and stuff over there man. You come, sure they want to hear you but they'll hear when you come play in those little dumps what they find for you to play in. Man, the last trip, I was over there with the quartet and we played at a place man down in one of them caves. There wasn't but one way out and that's the way you came in there. If anything would have happened down there, whew, it would be too bad, man. And you'd die in there playing, smoky. Everybody is smoking and you're down playing in this hole down there and there's no air, man, and you're inhaling all this stale air and smoke and you can't hardly breathe and you're playing, you're sweating, damp down there, from the humidity and your instrument is all tough, you know....
Yeah, yeah. I had to play some of them. I couldn't believe it.
I said if you let me get back to Teaneck this time, you know; in fact just let me get back and I ain't been back to Europe since and I ain't going.
Every year they want me, want us to come back over there and Cedar's going back over there, man. I refused it man. I'm not going to go and play in those dumps.
If I go, so I give them a price that will make them refuse me, you see. And I think I'm worth $1,500 plus hotel per

If you want me to come over there to play then give me $1,500 a week and hotel and I'll come over there and play for you. But under that I stay right here in my chair and watch cable, play my records. I can get a few gallons of gas and cross the bridge and go over there, you know what I mean.
And my wife works, she can put a few biscuits in the kitchen. I'm happy man right here.
I don't have to go for that stuff
